lead.headline: Mendoza mistakes a haunting for a strategy
lead.dek: Mendozareamazingpicks won by 2.88 while two starters made the scoreboard go bump in the wrong direction.
body: Mendoza is going to learn all the wrong lessons from this haunting. Mendozareamazingpicks beat Split Safety Syndicate 116.60–113.72 while Spencer Shrader and San Francisco’s defense each scored minus one. Two starting spots actively worked against the rest of the lineup, which is usually when someone suggests leaving the house.

Shrader made 1 of 3 field goals against Minnesota, and San Francisco allowed 29 points against Atlanta. Mendoza still finished with the week’s lowest winning score. Three losing teams scored more, which suggests everyone else wasted time setting lineups instead of choosing better opponents.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown. Rhamondre Stevenson added 5 catches for 93 yards and a score. Their combined 53.80 points covered the damage, so they should get to inspect the lineup for suspicious noises before anyone else touches it.

Mendoza then replaced Shrader with Tyler Bass, which shows a disappointing lack of commitment to the haunting. If losing points helped secure this win, the next kicker should lose even more. Mendoza should DOUBLE DOWN and hire a poltergeist to handle the subtraction.

rankings.take: Dak Side led the weekly scoring while Burrow threw four touchdowns. Baltimore’s defense scored minus-two in the same lineup, because apparently the league leader wanted to supply its own spooky noises.
Mendoza won with two negative starters and then replaced the kicker. Smith-Njigba and Stevenson supplied 53.80, so they should handle personnel decisions until everyone else stops subtracting.
Judkins ran for two touchdowns while Ted Hurst contributed zero. Shough won by 33.34, which will only encourage the belief that a receiver covered in cobwebs improves the spacing.
Pollard scored 36.50 without starting, and hammball won anyway. This team is leaving spare touchdowns in the attic while Rams of Steel look for a candle.
Jefferson scored 8.40 at Superflex while Cousins threw two touchdowns. The extra quarterback position apparently came with a strict one-quarterback limit that nobody else received.
Noel caught two passes for minus-three yards in our starting lineup. We recruited a receiver who could make the furniture move backward, then remembered we needed an offense.
Flowers and McBride combined for 54.80 against Rams of Steel. Micah carried a zero at kicker just to give the beating a decorative weakness.
Split leads the league in season scoring but sits eighth in Elo. Seattle’s defense followed instructions and stopped Split’s Kansas City players, so the haunting was coming from inside the lineup.
Burden needed four catches for 130 yards, while Concepcion needed eight for 129. Skat is one bad conclusion away from imposing a catch limit and calling it efficiency.
Jalon Daniels rushed twice for minus-three yards at Superflex. Kingslayers found the creaky stairs beneath the quarterback slot and immediately started exploring.
Jeanty caught every target and still couldn’t get this team a win. ThePeopleBeaters need fewer satisfied receivers and more disappointed opponents.
Caleb Williams supplied 308 passing yards and two touchdowns. Losing by 66.38 anyway suggests the rest of the lineup spent the evening hiding behind him with a flashlight.

recaps.headline: Skat gets through the haunted house in four catches
recaps.body: Skat is making a dangerous case for doing less work. Skat’s BruteForce Theorem beat ThePeopleBeaters by 31.16 behind Luther Burden III’s 4 catches, 130 yards and a touchdown. Chicago beat New England 30–24, while KC Concepcion Jr. added 8 catches for 129 yards against Tennessee. Ashton Jeanty caught all eight targets and scored through the air for ThePeopleBeaters, who still lost. Concepcion doubled Burden’s catch total and finished one yard behind him. Skat will probably hang a “Four catches only” sign over the door and claim that a fifth reception summons a curse.

recaps.headline: Dak Side gives the poltergeist a throwing lesson
recaps.body: Dak Side is making the obvious plan look annoyingly effective. Dak Side of the Sun started Joe Burrow and Dak Prescott, who threw 4 and 3 touchdowns respectively. Burrow passed for 292 yards against Baltimore, while Prescott added 212 against Philadelphia. J’Allen Waffle Stompers got 148 receiving yards and a touchdown from Tee Higgins, but Justin Jefferson supplied 8.40 at Superflex. Dak Side won by 20.16. If a receiver takes the extra quarterback chair, he should at least have to throw something before sitting down. Even a mediocre poltergeist can manage a lamp.

recaps.headline: Kingslayers open the door marked Do Not Enter
recaps.body: Kingslayers saw the creaky basement door and decided it looked promising. They scored a league-low 90.70 against WELL! It's The Big Shough as Jalon Daniels lost three yards on two carries. Jeremiyah Love and Romeo Doubs both scored zero. Shough got 96 rushing yards and 2 touchdowns from Quinshon Judkins, plus Colston Loveland’s 7 catches, 69 yards and a score. Ted Hurst contributed zero to Shough’s lineup, which Kingslayers apparently treated as a challenge. A zero should be the floor, but Kingslayers insisted on investigating the noises underneath it and bringing their quarterback along.

recaps.headline: Micah brings a haunted lineup with one harmless room
recaps.body: Rams of Steel found the harmless room in Micah’s haunted house and spent the rest of the matchup wishing it were bigger. Micah parsons fan club won 157.78–91.40 as Zay Flowers caught 8 passes for 137 yards and a touchdown. Trey McBride added 10 catches, 111 yards and a score, bringing their combined fantasy total to 54.80. Caleb Williams gave the Rams 308 passing yards and two touchdowns, but the game still ended with a 66.38-point gap. Micah even carried Trey Smack’s zero through the win. The Rams could relax at kicker; everywhere else, the furniture was moving.

recaps.headline: hammball keeps another offense in the attic
recaps.body: hammball brought an unreasonable amount of spare football to this matchup. It beat Unsportsmanlike Conduct 160.78–126.36 while another 108.18 points sat outside the starting lineup. Bucky Irving ran for 106 yards and two touchdowns, and CeeDee Lamb caught two scores in Dallas’s 38–21 win. UC got 321 passing yards and three total touchdowns from Drake Maye, while our Jaylin Noel caught two passes for minus-three yards. One team had touchdowns it couldn’t use; we had completions we wanted to return. Those nonstarter points should have to stay in the attic with the other things nobody wants to hear moving around after a loss.

recaps.headline: Split Safety hires a ghost to haunt its own lineup
recaps.body: Split Safety should check the address before hiring anyone to haunt a lineup. Split Safety Syndicate started Seattle’s defense against its own Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III and Travis Kelce. Seattle allowed 3 points and 213 yards in a 20–3 win, while Mahomes threw for 165 yards without a touchdown. Mendoza’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 passes for 150 yards and a score. The defense earned Split 11.00, but Mendoza still won by 2.88. Hiring Seattle to shut down Kansas City and then needing those Chiefs to score is how you end up paying the ghost to rattle your own windows.

awards.name: Manager of the Week
awards.body: Burrow threw 4 touchdowns and Prescott threw 3 more as Dak Side posted the week’s top score. This award should require something more complicated than remembering that quarterbacks can play quarterback. Unfortunately, the rest of the league keeps treating the depth chart like a door it is afraid to open.

awards.name: Least Necessary Touchdowns
awards.body: Pollard ran 25 times for 129 yards and 3 touchdowns, but hammball won without those 36.50 points. Leaving that many touchdowns unused while Rams of Steel struggle is like putting a full candy bowl in the window and refusing to answer the door. The neighbors are entitled to complain.

awards.name: Floor of the Week
awards.body: Puka Nacua caught 8 passes for 68 yards and a touchdown, while Stafford threw three scores in the same Rams win. Kingslayers still finished last in weekly fantasy scoring. Apparently the rest of the lineup thought standing perfectly still was the best way to avoid attracting a ghost.

awards.name: Best Performance in a Loss
awards.body: Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards, threw two touchdowns and ran for another. His 27.44 led every starter on a losing fantasy team, but UC still lost by 34.42. Giving him a trophy for this feels like thanking the person who found the flashlight while everyone else insists the strange noises are probably fine.

waivers.note: Shough spent $51 while ThePeopleBeaters lost with a $17 bid. At that price, Douglas should come with someone to carry the candle.
UC released Dowdle on Sunday and then bid $3 to reclaim him. The Rams paid $27, so our haunted revolving door has finally delivered someone to a different house.
UC paid $11 for Bourne after its receivers made ordinary forward movement look like a special skill. He only needs to get past the cobwebs to improve the atmosphere.
Houston has a bye next week, while Cincinnati hosts Tennessee. UC has correctly identified playing an actual game as a useful defensive trait.
Mendoza paid $3 to replace Shrader after he made one of three field goals. UC’s zero-dollar bid failed, proving that even evicting minus-one from a haunted lineup requires a deposit.
Shough dropped Cleveland for Jacksonville, which returns from its bye against Indianapolis. The $3 purchase left considerably more money than the Caleb Douglas decision.

transactions.free_agents_label: Free-agent moves · 15 total, including two drop-only moves

free_agents.note: ThePeopleBeaters added McCarthy on October 21, and he later started with 252 passing yards and no passing touchdown. Finding a quarterback did not automatically find a rescue.
ThePeopleBeaters added Strong on October 21 and dropped him for Keenan Allen the following day. Even the ghost at the door barely had time to learn his name.
ThePeopleBeaters added Flournoy on October 21. He caught all four targets for 70 yards but remained outside their lineup.
The Waffle Stompers added Knight on October 22. He later ran seven times for 48 yards and caught three passes for 15 without making their starting lineup.
Skat added Bell on October 22 and kept him outside the lineup. Bell finished with three receptions for 25 yards.
ThePeopleBeaters added Allen on October 22, and he finished with three catches for 31 yards. The receiver shopping produced another player to watch from outside the lineup.
UC added Meyers on October 22 while Jacksonville was on bye. We were shopping for next week while this week was still rattling the windows.
UC added Fields on October 22, and he caught four passes for 83 yards outside our starting lineup. Useful football rang the doorbell, and apparently we assumed it was another ghost.
Shough added Hunter and released Samaje Perine on October 22 Eastern.
The Rams added Cooper on October 24 Eastern and started him. His one catch for 17 yards suggests that completing the transaction was the exciting part.
UC added Noel on October 25 and started him. He caught two passes for minus-three yards. Next time we will specify that we want the ordinary kind of possession.
Kingslayers dropped Kalif Raymond on October 25 without making a corresponding addition.
Shough dropped Chris Boswell on October 27 Eastern after he made all three field goals in Paris. Apparently perfection needed to happen somewhere less inconvenient.
Kingslayers dropped Indianapolis for the Rams on October 28 ahead of the Chargers matchup.
UC added Stevens at 7:49 a.m. Eastern on October 28 and dropped Fairbairn before Houston’s bye. The move arrived 11 minutes before the coverage window closed.

preview.note: Houston, New Orleans, the Giants and San Francisco have Week 8 byes. Carolina visits Green Bay on Thursday night, so everyone has time to check a lineup before blaming the strange noises in the house.

games.line: Skat comes off a 154.86-point week before facing the Waffle Stompers. The four-catch theory belongs in a dusty book nobody should read aloud near the lineup settings.
Both teams are 2-5, so ThePeopleBeaters and Kingslayers finally have a chance to make one of those names sound accurate.
Dak Side leads Elo while the Rams sit last. An upset here would justify checking the rankings machine for an unusually mischievous ghost.
Shough faces hammball’s starters after the nonstarters spent this week showing off. Everyone should confirm which group is actually allowed out of the attic.

Mendoza meets Micah after winning with 116.60. Bringing a functioning kicker would be a reasonable way to prepare for an opponent that just scored 157.78, although Mendoza may prefer another haunted experiment.
Split and UC both just lost, and Seattle faces Chicago next. Split can therefore support its own quarterbacks without hiring a defense to argue back.
